text: Which HTML tag is used to create a hyperlink?
explanation: <a> (anchor) tag creates hyperlinks using the href attribute. <link> is for CSS stylesheets, <href> and <url> are not valid HTML tags.

text: What does HTML stand for?
explanation: HTML stands for Hyper Text Markup Language. 'Hyper' refers to hyperlinks, 'Text' is the content type, 'Markup' means tagging, 'Language' is the syntax system.

text: Which attribute specifies an alternate text for an image in HTML?
explanation: The 'alt' attribute provides alternate text for images when they cannot be displayed. 'src' specifies the image source, 'title' shows tooltip text, 'name' is used for form elements.

text: Which HTML tag is used to define a table row?
explanation: <tr> defines a table row. <td> defines a table data cell, <th> defines a table header cell, and <table> is the container for the entire table.

text: Which input type creates a password field in HTML?
explanation: type='password' masks the input characters. type='text' shows plain text, type='hidden' hides the field entirely, type='secure' is not a valid HTML input type.

text: What does IP stand for in networking?
explanation: IP stands for Internet Protocol, the fundamental protocol governing the internet. It handles addressing and routing of data packets between devices.

text: What is the full form of LAN?
explanation: LAN stands for Local Area Network — a network covering a small geographical area like an office or building. WAN covers wide areas, MAN covers metropolitan areas.

text: Which device is used to connect two different networks?
explanation: A Router connects different networks and routes data packets between them. A Hub/Switch works within the same network, and a Repeater only amplifies signals without connecting different networks.

text: Which keyboard shortcut is used to save a document in MS Word?
explanation: Ctrl+S saves the document. Ctrl+P is for Print, Ctrl+X is for Cut, Alt+S is not a standard save shortcut in MS Word.

text: What is the extension of an MS Excel file?
explanation: .xls (or .xlsx) is the MS Excel file extension. .doc is MS Word, .ppt is MS PowerPoint, .txt is plain text file.

text: Which tag is used to make text bold in HTML?
explanation: <b> makes text bold. <i> makes text italic, <u> underlines text, and <em> emphasizes text (usually rendered as italic, but has semantic meaning).

text: What is the correct HTML tag for inserting a line break?
explanation: inserts a line break in HTML. , , and are not valid HTML tags.

text: Which attribute of the form tag specifies where to send form data?
explanation: The 'action' attribute specifies the URL where form data is sent. 'method' specifies GET/POST method, 'target' specifies where to display response, 'name' identifies the form.

text: Which HTML tag creates an unordered (bulleted) list?
explanation: <ul> creates an unordered list with bullets. <ol> creates an ordered (numbered) list, <li> defines each list item, <list> is not a valid HTML tag.

text: What does DNS stand for?
explanation: DNS stands for Domain Name System — it translates human-readable domain names (like www.google.com) into IP addresses that computers use to communicate.

text: Which protocol is used for sending emails?
explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used for sending emails. FTP transfers files, HTTP transfers web pages, and POP3 is used for receiving/downloading emails.

text: What is the maximum number of computers that can be connected in a bus topology?
explanation: Bus topology allows as many computers as the cable can handle (limited by hardware constraints like cable length and signal degradation), not a fixed number like 10 or 100.

text: Which function key opens Help in MS Office applications?
explanation: F1 opens the Help menu in most MS Office applications. F2 renames selected items, F5 finds/replaces or refreshes, F10 activates the menu bar.

text: In MS Excel, which function returns the sum of a range of cells?
explanation: =SUM() is the correct Excel function to add values in a range. =ADD(), =TOTAL(), and =PLUS() are not valid Excel functions.

text: What is the cell address of the cell in the 3rd column and 2nd row of an Excel worksheet?
explanation: In Excel, columns are labeled with letters and rows with numbers. The 3rd column is C, the 2nd row is 2, so the cell address is C2. B3 would be 2nd column, 3rd row.

text: What is an algorithm?
options: A step-by-step procedure to solve a problem
explanation: An algorithm is a step-by-step, finite set of instructions to solve a problem. It is not a programming language, hardware, or database system.

text: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a good algorithm?
explanation: Ambiguity is NOT a characteristic of a good algorithm. Good algorithms must be Finite (end after finite steps), Definite (clear instructions), Effective (each step is achievable), and Input/Output defined.

text: What is the time complexity of a linear search algorithm?
explanation: Linear search has O(n) time complexity — it checks each element one by one. O(1) is constant time, O(log n) is binary search, O(n²) is for algorithms like bubble sort.

text: Which attribute is used to merge cells horizontally in an HTML table?
explanation: 'colspan' merges cells horizontally (across columns). 'rowspan' merges cells vertically (across rows). 'cellspan' and 'merge' are not valid HTML table attributes.

text: What does the <head> tag in HTML contain?
options: Meta information and links to stylesheets
explanation: <head> contains meta information (title, charset, description), links to stylesheets, and scripts — not visible body content. Visible content goes in <body>.

text: What does DBMS stand for?
explanation: DBMS stands for Database Management System — software for creating, managing, and organizing databases. Examples include MySQL, Oracle, MS Access.

text: In a relational database, what is a primary key?
options: A column that uniquely identifies each row
The first column of a table
explanation: A primary key uniquely identifies each row/record in a table. It cannot be NULL or duplicate. It is not necessarily the first column, and it's different from a foreign key.

text: Which topology connects all devices to a central hub?
explanation: In Star topology, all devices connect to a central hub or switch. Bus topology uses a single cable, Ring topology connects devices in a loop, Mesh connects each device to every other.

text: Which tab in MS Word contains the 'Font' group?
explanation: The 'Home' tab in MS Word contains the Font group with options for font type, size, bold, italic, etc. Insert is for adding objects, View controls display, References is for citations.

text: In MS Excel, what does the formula =IF(A1>10,"High","Low") return when A1=15?
explanation: Since A1=15 which is greater than 10, the IF condition is TRUE, so it returns "High". "Low" would be returned if A1 were 10 or less. The formula is valid so no Error is returned.

text: Which HTML tag defines the document type?
explanation: <!DOCTYPE html> declares the document type and version of HTML. <html> is the root element, <head> contains metadata, <meta> provides meta information.

text: Which input type creates radio buttons in HTML?
explanation: type='radio' creates radio buttons allowing single selection from options. type='checkbox' allows multiple selections, type='button' creates a clickable button, type='select' is not valid (use <select> tag instead).

text: What is the difference between IPv4 and IPv6?
options: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses; IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses
IPv4 supports more addresses than IPv6
explanation: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses (~4.3 billion), while IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses (vastly more). IPv6 is newer (not older) and supports far more addresses than IPv4.

text: What does HTTP stand for?
explanation: HTTP stands for Hyper Text Transfer Protocol — the foundation of data communication on the web. HTTPS adds the security layer (SSL/TLS).

text: What is a flowchart?
options: A graphical representation of an algorithm
explanation: A flowchart is a graphical/diagrammatic representation of an algorithm using standard symbols (ovals for start/end, rectangles for process, diamonds for decisions, parallelograms for I/O).

text: Which symbol is used for a decision in a flowchart?
explanation: A Diamond shape represents a decision (yes/no or true/false) in a flowchart. Rectangle is for processing steps, Oval is for Start/End, Parallelogram is for Input/Output.

text: What is a foreign key in a database?
options: A column that references the primary key of another table
The second column of a table
explanation: A foreign key is a column (or set of columns) that references the primary key of another table, establishing a relationship between the two tables.

text: In MS Word, which feature automatically corrects spelling mistakes?
explanation: AutoCorrect automatically corrects common spelling mistakes as you type. AutoFormat formats text automatically, AutoFill (Excel feature) fills in series, AutoText stores frequently used text.

text: What is the purpose of the VLOOKUP function in Excel?
options: To look up a value in the leftmost column and return a value in the same row from another column
explanation: VLOOKUP searches for a value in the first column of a range and returns a value in the same row from a specified column. It's used for data lookup/retrieval operations.

text: What does WWW stand for?
explanation: WWW stands for World Wide Web — the system of interlinked hypertext documents accessed via the Internet. It was invented by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989.

text: Which CSS property changes the text color?
explanation: The CSS property 'color' changes the text color. 'font-color' and 'text-color' are not valid CSS properties; 'foreground' is not a CSS property.

text: Which HTML attribute is used to specify an inline style for an element?
explanation: The 'style' attribute applies inline CSS directly to an HTML element. 'class' links to a CSS class, 'id' provides a unique identifier, 'css' is not a valid HTML attribute.

text: In a binary search algorithm, what is the prerequisite condition?
options: The list must contain unique elements
The list must be in descending order
The list must have an even number of elements
explanation: Binary search requires the list to be sorted (in ascending or descending order). It doesn't require unique elements, doesn't mandate descending order, and works with any number of elements.

text: What is the function of a firewall?
options: Monitors and controls incoming/outgoing network traffic based on security rules
Stores web pages for faster access
Converts domain names to IP addresses
explanation: A firewall monitors and controls network traffic based on predetermined security rules, blocking unauthorized access. Caching speeds access, DNS converts domain names, and a firewall doesn't inherently speed connections.

text: What is SQL?
options: Structured Query Language for managing relational databases
explanation: SQL stands for Structured Query Language — used to create, manipulate, and retrieve data from relational databases. It's not for hardware control and SQL stands for Structured, not Simple or Sequential.

text: In MS Excel, what does the AVERAGE function do?
options: Calculates the arithmetic mean of values
explanation: =AVERAGE() calculates the arithmetic mean (sum divided by count) of the specified values. MAX() returns maximum, MIN() returns minimum, COUNT() counts cells with numbers.

text: Which view in MS PowerPoint shows all slides as small thumbnails?
explanation: Slide Sorter View displays all slides as thumbnails, making it easy to rearrange slides. Normal View is the editing view, Reading View is for presentation review, Presenter View is for presenting with notes.

text: What is cloud computing?
options: Delivery of computing services over the internet
A type of weather prediction software
explanation: Cloud computing delivers computing services (servers, storage, databases, networking, software) over the internet ('the cloud'), enabling flexible resources and economies of scale without local infrastructure.

text: What is pseudocode?
options: An informal high-level description of an algorithm written in plain language
explanation: Pseudocode is an informal, high-level description of an algorithm using plain language mixed with programming constructs. It's used for planning algorithms before writing actual code, making it language-independent.

text: What is the purpose of the <meta charset='UTF-8'> tag?
options: Specifies the character encoding for the HTML document
explanation: <meta charset='UTF-8'> specifies UTF-8 character encoding, ensuring the browser correctly displays special characters, symbols, and international text. It has nothing to do with columns, file size, or font size.
